metadata.purpose: Ep. 13 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 13 (SETI and signal detection - how AI separates potential alien signals from human radio interference).
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 is the ONE accent and marks WHAT THE ASSUMPTION DECIDES - the injected signal's track, the recall that appears when the search is widened, the cadence test that does not depend on the guess. Ink marks WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE REGARDLESS - the interference standing vertical at zero drift, and the morphology search's own score. The mapping never flips, so B04 teaches it once. Accented text is #A44A32; #B9B4A0 is strokes and fills only.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Eps. 01-06 had AI inspecting observations; 07 standing in for a calculation; 08 a division of labour; 09 an output that was never a measurement; 10 a training set produced by past decisions; 11 an objective that omitted the failure; 12 an evaluation inflated by how the data was split. Ep. 13 is the first where THE POSITIVE CLASS DOES NOT EXIST. There is no training set to be biased, no objective to under-specify and no test set to leak, because nobody has ever observed the thing being searched for. The limit is therefore not a flaw in the method but a property of the question, and the only escape is a test that does not reference the hypothesis at all.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00, B11, B12, B13. Every other beat illustrates its concept as a reel-local Manim scene (scenes.py). Plates come from assets/gen_seti.py, which runs the REAL detection statistic - the de-Doppler sum a technosignature pipeline computes - so the episode's subject, the assumption, is a single visible number: the range of drift rates swept. THREE claims are ASSERTED and the script writes nothing if any fails. A FOURTH claim was measured and CUT: an earlier version argued zero drift is too crowded to search, but the measurement showed 6 look-alikes for a drifting candidate against 5 for a stationary one - no difference - and raising the interference count until the claim came true would be tuning the experiment to the conclusion. BLC1's look-alike argument therefore appears as a PUBLISHED result only. Seed 1313. No LaTeX/MathTex anywhere. metadata.channel_title is omitted for the GATE V edge-bleed reason logged in Ep. 03. scenes.py is ASPECT-AWARE and the three-panel plate ships in both arrangements (three / three_v).

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about how we search for alien radio signals, and why the thing we are searching for is something we made up.

show.event: the composer types the ask on the cream stage
the send button arms in terracotta
running indicator: sweeping 49 drift rates
three result lines land in order

props.command: SETI pipelines sift radio data for narrowband signals and now use deep learning to do it. What exactly are they trained to recognise, given that nobody has ever detected one?
output: the search assumes a form - the range of drift rates is the assumption
a transmitter that corrects its own drift: found 0 times in 80
the test that catches it asks WHERE, not WHAT

beats.narration_text: Twelve episodes of AI looking at things that exist. This one is about looking for something nobody has ever found.

show.event: OM MALI writes in, terracotta hairline underlines it
role line fades in: Humanitarians AI - presenter
a card draws beside it
row one lands and is STRUCK: twelve episodes / things that exist
row two lands boxed: this one / nobody has found it
series line: Ep. 13 - the positive class is imaginary

beats.narration_text: Here is the problem. We have never detected one. So to build a search, you have to assume what it looks like. And then you find what you assumed.

show.event: a card draws on the cream stage
line one types: WE HAVE NEVER DETECTED ONE, sub: not once, in sixty years
line two: SO YOU ASSUME A FORM, sub: there is nothing else to do
line three lands in the accent and is UNDERLINED: AND THEN YOU FIND IT
closer: the one you assumed

beats.narration_text: Two thousand nineteen. Parkes, pointed at Proxima Centauri. A narrow tone at nine eighty-two megahertz survives every cut and gets a name. Then they find dozens more just like it, from broken electronics on the ground.

show.event: a published-ledger chip lands: Nature Astronomy, 2021
a frequency axis draws; one terracotta tone stands on it
a card names it: BLC1, Breakthrough Listen Candidate 1
dozens of ink tones appear along the axis around it
the terracotta tone turns ink: it was one of them
closer: dozens of look-alikes

beats.narration_text: This is what the data looks like. Time down, frequency across. The dark vertical lines are us, transmitters on the ground. A signal from the sky leans, because the planet moves. A faint one is invisible here, which is why you integrate.

show.event: waterfall.png fades in
axis labels land: time down, frequency across
two vertical interference lines are ringed and named: us
the terracotta leaning track is traced
a chip lands: and you cannot see it
closer: which is why you integrate

beats.narration_text: So that is the search. Try every lean, keep the best. The range of leans you try is the assumption, written as a number. Anything outside it is not missed. It is never looked for.

show.event: an empty panel draws
a fan of trial tracks sweeps across it, one at a time
one track lights terracotta: the best
a bracket closes around the fan: the searched range
a vertical track OUTSIDE the bracket greys out
closer: never looked for

beats.narration_text: Here are three transmitters. One leans, like we assume. One corrects its own drift, which is what we do. One blinks. All three are things a transmitter can do.

show.event: three.png lands: three fields side by side
panel one is named: leans - what we assume
panel two: corrects its own drift - what we do
panel three: blinks
closer: all three are things a transmitter can do

beats.narration_text: Run the search. The one that leans, found every time. The one that corrects its drift, found never — zero out of eighty. Widen the search by one number, and it is found every time.

show.event: recall.png: six bars, the first pair already high
the middle ink bar is ringed - it is flat on the axis
a counter lands: 0 of 80
the middle terracotta bar is ringed: 80 of 80
closer: one number, the whole difference

beats.narration_text: And you can watch the blind spot appear. Move the edge of the search outward, and recall falls off a cliff exactly where it crosses zero.

show.event: edge.png draws: recall against the search's lower edge
the curve is followed from the left
the cliff is marked
a chip lands at the foot: 0.06 Hz per second
closer: that is the whole blind spot

beats.narration_text: So use a different test. Point at the star. Look away. Point back. Look away. A signal from the sky comes and goes with the telescope. Interference does not care where you point.

show.event: cadence.png: six traces, three and three
the left column is named: pointed at the star
a peak is ringed in each left trace
the right column is named: pointed away
the right traces stay flat
closer: it comes and goes with the telescope

beats.narration_text: So the tell. That test does not care what the signal looks like. The one our search scores zero on, it finds three times in four. Ask where it came from, not what it resembles.

show.event: compare.png: morphology against cadence, three pairs
the middle ink bar is flat on the axis again
the middle terracotta bar stands at three quarters
a bracket joins them: 0 to 0.76
closer: ask where it came from

beats.narration_text: So: we have never seen one. Every search is a guess about form. The only test that escapes the guess is the one that asks where it came from.

show.event: the artefact page opens on the cream stage
line one lands
line two lands
line three lands
line four lands
line five lands in the accent

props.artifactTitle: The Signal We Imagined - one page
props.artifactHeading: You find the one you assumed
artifactLines: Nobody has ever detected a radio technosignature, so the positive class is hypothetical.
To build a search you assume a form - and the range of drift rates you sweep IS that assumption.
A transmitter that corrects its own Doppler, which is what we do for spacecraft, was found 0 times in 80.
Widen the search by one number and it is found 80 times in 80. The blind spot was the parameter.
The test that escapes this asks where a signal came from, not what it looks like.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Read it. Here is what my detector was trained to recognise. Tell me what it would miss, and what test would catch that without me having to guess right first.

show.event: the composer types the handoff prompt
the send button arms
three grading lines land

props.command: Here is exactly what my detector was trained to recognise. Tell me what it would miss, and design a test that would catch that without me having to guess the right form first.
output: grade it: does it name something OUTSIDE the training form
grade it: is the test independent of appearance
grade it: could you run it with the data you already have
